result.topic_en: Euler shows that the equation for the vibration frequencies has no root in the first quadrant or in any even quadrant, then locates the first root in the third quadrant at approximately ω = 225°.

$\text{ſin.}\,\omega\,(e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}) = 2\,\omega\,(1+\tfrac{1}{3}\,\omega\omega-\tfrac{1}{30}\,\omega^{4})$ et
$\text{coſ.}\,\omega\,(e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega}) = 2\,\omega\,(1-\tfrac{1}{3}\,\omega\omega-\tfrac{1}{30}\,\omega^{4})$;
vnde patet, priorem formulam per totum primum quadrantem maiorem eſſe quam poſteriorem, ita vt in hoc quadrante nullus reperiatur valor pro angulo $\omega$. In ſecundo autem quadrante, vbi omnes tangentes ſunt negatiui, nullus iterum dari poteſt, neque etiam in quarto, ſexto, octavo et omnibus paribus. Reliquos quadrantes in corollariis percurramus.

Corollarium 1.

§. 24. Conſideremus igitur tertium quadrantem, vbi, cum ſit $\omega$ maius quam $\pi$, formula $\frac{e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega}}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}}$ parum ab vnitate deficiet, vnde angulus $\omega$ aliquanto minor erit quam $\pi+45^{\circ}$. Hinc ſumto iterum $\varrho$ pro ſigno anguli recti ſtatuamus $\omega=\pi+\tfrac{1}{2}\varrho-\Phi$, eritque
$\text{tang.}\,\omega = \text{tang.}\,(\tfrac{1}{2}\varrho-\Phi) = \frac{1-\text{tang.}\,\Phi}{1+\text{tang.}\,\Phi}$.
Cum igitur ſit
$\frac{1-\text{tang.}\,\Phi}{1+\text{tang.}\,\Phi} = \frac{e^{\omega}-e^{-\omega}}{e^{\omega}+e^{-\omega}} = \frac{1-e^{-2\omega}}{1+e^{-2\omega}}$,
hinc manifeſto eſt $\text{tang.}\,\Phi = e^{-2\omega} = \frac{1}{e^{2\pi+\varrho-2\Phi}}$, in quo exponente angulum exiguum $\Phi$ negligere licet, ita vt ſubducto calculo reperiatur $\text{tang.}\,\Phi = \frac{1}{2576}$; ſicque angulus $\Phi$ vix vnum minutum ſuperat, id quod tuto negligi poteſt, ita vt primus valor ſit $\omega=\pi+\tfrac{1}{2}\varrho=225^{\circ}$, cuius tam ſinus quam coſinus eſt $=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

items.english: Whence it is evident that the former formula is greater than the latter throughout the whole first quadrant, so that no value of the angle ω is found in this quadrant.

items.quote: In ſecundo autem quadrante, vbi omnes tangentes ſunt negatiui, nullus iterum dari poteſt, neque etiam in quarto, ſexto, octavo et omnibus paribus.
items.english: In the second quadrant, however, where all tangents are negative, again none can be given, nor in the fourth, sixth, eighth and all even quadrants.
Let us run through the remaining quadrants in the corollaries.
